title: Redwood cost econ discovery - Harrow Capital
summary: Intro discovery focused on per-token economics for Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer has budget constraints (approx $20k/mo initial), heavy throughput for batch scoring, and latency SLOs for some features. Discussed batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization, and potential pilot/benchmark. Agreed next steps: send cost model, run benchmark with sample workload, and share security docs.
topics: Current infra + clouds, expected qps and token/sec, batching strategies, prefix/K V cache, Dedicated reserved capacity pricing, pilot scope and success metrics, security/compliance (KMS, audit logs, SSO).
action_items: Ava: send tailored cost-model spreadsheet and public pricing link by 2026-03-06
Diego: share benchmark script and recommended batching/cache config; propose pilot cluster size by 2026-03-09
Harrow (James): provide a 24h sample of scoring traffic and top 100 prompt templates by 2026-03-07
next_steps: Send tailored cost model spreadsheet and sample pricing scenarios
Schedule 2-week pilot / benchmark run (hosted + dedicated) w/ sample data
Share SOC2 + security + private deployment docs
Follow-up call to review benchmark results and draft SOW
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ava with Redwood — Diego and I are here to talk cost economics and how we might help Harrow.
[00:12] James Whitman: Thanks, Ava. Quick background — we've got two main workloads, one is high-volume batch scoring (overnight + streaming) and one is a low-latency chat feature for a small set of users. Budget is roughly 20k a month to start, we can scale.
[00:28] Diego Morales: Cool, can you give ballpark qps and average token lengths? That helps us pick model family and batching levers.
[00:35] Sofia Patel: For batch scoring it's about 200k requests/day, avg 120 tokens per request. Chat is maybe 30 qps peak, 40 tokens per turn.
[00:44] Ravi Kapoor: We're on GCP primarily, small footprint on AWS for DR. We need VPC peering and customer-managed K M S for keys if possible.
[00:56] Ava Chen: Got it, thanks. So main levers we'll talk about: per-token pricing (hosted), reserved capacity for Dedicated (predictable unit costs), and operational levers — batching, prefix/K V caching, and quantization to reduce cost.
[01:11] James: Walk me through how batching actually reduces per-token cost — is it just GPU throughput efficiency?
[01:18] Diego: Yeah mostly — continuous batching consolidates many small requests into a larger matrix pass which amortizes kernel startup and memory bandwidth. You get higher tokens/sec and lower cost/token. But there's latency tradeoffs — we set burst/latency SLOs per route.
[01:34] Sofia: And caching, you mean prefix caching? like reusing KV cache between similar requests?
[01:40] Diego: Exactly. Prefix or KV cache stores previous key/value states for repeated prefixes so you don't re-run the entire prompt. For embeddings or templated prompts that saves a lot. There is an overhead to manage the cache, but for repeated patterns it's huge.
[01:52] James: Any numbers — ballpark percent savings?
[01:55] Ava: Typical for templated prompts we've seen 30-70% token reduction after cache hits; for heavy batching it depends on seq length but 2-4x effective throughput isn't uncommon.
[02:08] Ravi: For Dedicated what's the pricing model? Do we get a per-token discount or flat GPU reservation? We're trying to know when Dedicated makes sense versus hosted.
[02:16] Ava: Dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly/annual). You pay for the pool (GPUs + orchestration) and get lower unit costs because of utilization and no managed per-token premium. For your volumes, if you can sustain higher baseline throughput, Dedicated often comes in cheaper per-token. We usually model both scenarios.
[02:31] James: Does Dedicated support our K M S and V P C requirements?
[02:34] Diego: Yes — Dedicated or Private deployments can be in your V P C with customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs. There's an on-prem option if you need air-gapped, though that has different ops overhead.
[02:45] Sofia: How do we model the tradeoff? We have variable batch sizes overnight and spikes during the day.
[02:50] Ava: We'll run a cost-model: inputs are token volumes, peak qps, percent cache hits, target latency SLOs. We compare Hosted per-token pricing with estimated batching/caching savings vs Dedicated reserved cost + utilization assumptions. We'll include sensitivity analysis — e.g., if cache hit rate is 20% vs 50% how unit cost changes.
[03:06] James: Can you talk about quantization and model variants? Are smaller models an easy way to save money?
[03:12] Diego: Model family has big impact. Quantized models (4-bit/8-bit) run much cheaper on GPU, sometimes with small accuracy regressions depending on tasks. We can recommend model+quantization combos for embeddings vs generation. Also routing rules: use cheaper model for low-criticality routes and fallback to larger models for critical queries.
[03:29] Sofia: Sounds good. For the pilot — what do you need from us to run an apples-to-apples benchmark?
[03:34] Ava: A 24h sample of traffic (anonymized), top prompt templates, and success metrics: p50/p95 latency targets, quality thresholds (acceptible BLEU/ROUGE or human eval), and budget cap for pilot. Diego will provide the benchmark script.
[03:47] Ravi: Security question — what's Redwood's encryption at rest and in transit? Can we bring our own keys?
[03:52] Diego: TLS everywhere in transit. For Hosted we encrypt at rest and can integrate with customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private. We also provide audit logs and per-token access traces. We'll share SOC2 and ISO docs.
[04:05] James: Any gotchas around billing? If we burst above the reserved pool, how are tokens billed?
[04:09] Ava: We have burst capacity options — depending on your contract, bursts can be billed at a slightly higher unit rate or draw from hosted pool. We'll model the blended rate.
[04:17] Sofia: Are there hidden costs for egress or data transfer between cloud regions?
[04:20] Diego: Good point — data egress follows cloud provider fees; for Dedicated inside your V P C that's minimized but inter-region traffic still incurs provider egress. We'll note that in the model.
[04:31] James: For our batch scoring, what batching config would you recommend? We run 120-token avg; 200k requests/day.
[04:36] Diego: For that profile, a medium-large batch window with dynamic micro-batching during peaks. We might aim for batch sizes that hit GPU utilization targets — I'll include recommended batch size range and expected latency impact in the doc. Also prefix caching if templates repeat.
[04:50] Sofia: If the pilot shows Dedicated is cheaper, how long to provision a Dedicated pool?
[04:54] Ava: Provisioning can be quick for cloud-hosted Dedicated (days) but we usually plan 2-4 weeks for sizing, security reviews, and networking. Private/on-prem takes longer.
[05:03] James: Ok great. Any competitors we should worry about? We've looked at Anthropic and Replicate for custom infra.
[05:09] Ava: Yes, Anthropic for model access and Replicate for self-hosting workflows are common alternatives. We emphasize our observability and cost tooling as a differentiator.
[05:18] Ravi: One more — can Redwood show token-level cost breakdown by route? We want to tag routes by product and get per-feature P&L.
[05:24] Diego: Yup — our Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model. You can annotate routes to cost centers.
[05:31] Ava: Cool — recap of next steps: we'll send the cost-model spreadsheet, Diego will share the benchmark and recommended configs, and Harrow will share sample traffic. We'll schedule the benchmark start next week.
[05:42] James: Sounds good — appreciate the walkthrough.
[05:45] Sofia: Thanks everyone.
[05:47] Ava: Thanks, talk soon.
